hero: A crowded pediatric ward in a Philippine provincial hospital during a dengue outbreak, monsoon rain on the windows. A Filipino pediatric nephrologist listens with a stethoscope to the back of a 10-year-old girl sitting up in bed with a nasal cannula. Her father, in a work shirt, stands at the foot of the bed holding her slippers. A nurse checks an intravenous pump. Several other beds with mosquito nets in the background. No text.

figures.teaches: Stage AKI from both creatinine and urine output, and calculate percentage fluid overload daily.
figures.content: Left half: table 'KDIGO 2012 stages'. Stage 1: '1.5-1.9x baseline or +0.3 mg/dL' / '<0.5 mL/kg/h 6-12 h'. Stage 2: '2.0-2.9x' / '<0.5 mL/kg/h >=12 h'. Stage 3: '>=3x, >=4.0 mg/dL, KRT, or eGFR <35 under 18' / '<0.3 mL/kg/h >=24 h or anuria >=12 h'. Right half: formula box '% fluid overload = (fluid in - fluid out, L) / admission weight (kg) x 100'. Worked example: 'Weight 32 kg to 35.2 kg = 10%'. Footer: 'Creatinine alone missed 67.2% (AWARE)'.

figures.teaches: Fluid helps during the dengue leak and harms during reabsorption; falling hematocrit with shock means bleeding.
figures.content: Horizontal timeline in three colored bands: 'Febrile', 'Critical (leak)', 'Recovery (reabsorption)'. Above: hematocrit line rising in the critical band and falling in recovery. Middle: capillary icon with arrows outward in critical, inward in recovery. Below each band: 'Oral fluids', 'Fluid by protocol', 'Stop or reduce fluid'. Red warning box on the recovery band: 'Falling hematocrit + shock = bleeding: give blood'. Small note: 'Dengue AKI: 0.9% of admissions, 64% died (Thai cohort)'.

card: A Filipino girl sitting up in a hospital bed under a mosquito net, rain on the window, her father beside her holding her hand.
